judgments.comparative_verdict: Both reports are essentially equivalent — each hits all four expectations with correct root cause, commit, reproduction path, and next-step assessment; Report 2 is slightly crisper on isolation/shadow-run but the difference is marginal.

report_1.evidence: `ticket-scorer/config/scoring_config.yaml` (line 2) says `expected_label_field: label`, but every record in `ticket-scorer/fixtures/eval_set.jsonl` stores its gold label under the key `gold_label`. The batch scorer, `ticket-scorer/pipeline/score_batch.py`, looks the gold label up with `gold = record.get(gold_field)` (line 47), and `dict.get` on a missing key silently returns `None`.

report_2.evidence: Its line `expected_label_field: label` names a field that no longer exists in the evaluation set: since 2026-06-17, every record in `fixtures/eval_set.jsonl` keys its gold answer as `gold_label`. The batch scorer (`pipeline/score_batch.py:47`) looks the gold answer up with `record.get(gold_field)`, and `dict.get` returns `None` for a missing key instead of raising

report_1.evidence: introduced by commit **`53551e8` — "chore(eval): migrate eval set to gold_label schema (SCORE-77)"**... it renamed `"label"` to `"gold_label"` in all 11 records of `fixtures/eval_set.jsonl`... `pipeline/metrics/nightly_scores.csv` shows 0.91 on 2026-06-16 and 0.00 on 2026-06-17 — the exact day the commit landed

report_2.evidence: introduced by commit **`53551e8` — "chore(eval): migrate eval set to gold_label schema (SCORE-77)"**... `pipeline/metrics/nightly_scores.csv` shows 0.91 on 2026-06-16 and 0.00 on 2026-06-17 and every night since; (b) `git show 53551e8` shows the commit renamed `"label"` to `"gold_label"` in all 11 rows of `fixtures/eval_set.jsonl`

report_1.evidence: `pipeline/score_one.py` only runs the prediction half of the pipeline — `predict_category(normalize_simple(text))` — and never loads the config, never loads the eval set, and never compares against a gold label... The correct reproduction is: (a) run the batch entrypoint itself rather than the single-item tool

report_2.evidence: `pipeline/score_one.py` never loads the config and never compares against a gold label — it only prints the classifier's prediction... The correct reproduction is: run the same entry point the nightly job runs, `pipeline/score_batch.py`, against the checked-in config and eval set

report_1.evidence: The failure mode is structural: `prediction == None` is false for every possible prediction, so accuracy stays 0.00 under any model, old or new. After the rollback "experiment," the score would remain 0.00, which the team would likely misread as "the old model is broken too"

report_2.evidence: flipping the model on the shared nightly environment to "confirm whether the score recovers" is experimenting on production; a candidate should run in a shadow/parallel lane instead... no model change can move the number
